senses.note: often used with à or en

stems.note: j'habite, ils habitent (sources attest elle habite, ils habitent).

conjugations.formation_note: Present subjunctive uses the same stem as the present indicative.
Imperative = present forms without the subject pronoun.

sources.source_text: Cette famille habite ici depuis longtemps.

sources.section_title: Uses of the imparfait: habitual and repetitive action
sources.source_text: À cette époque, ils (habiter) en banlieue.

usage_notes: « Habiter » may take a place directly (« habiter Paris ») or be followed by « à », « en », or « dans » depending on the type of location.

related_grammar_rules: Preposition with countries: en, au, aux
transformations: masculine countries take au instead : au Canada

sources.source_text: Ils ont acheté une maison en Sicile.

related_grammar_rules: Preposition with cities: à
transformations: no contraction with city names : à Hanoi, à Paris
alternative without a preposition : habiter Paris

related_grammar_rules: Preposition with countries: en, au, aux
transformations: de + le → du for the origin : du Canada

related_grammar_rules: Preposition with countries: en, au, aux
transformations: de + les → des for the origin : des États-Unis

usage_notes: Use en France for 'in/to France' and de France for 'from/of France'.
Use au Canada for 'in/to Canada' and du Canada for 'from/of Canada'.
The country name is plural: « les États-Unis »; use the contraction « aux États-Unis » after « à ».

grammar_rules.summary: Use à to express in/to for cities.
grammar_rules.explanation: Cities generally do not take an article and use à.
usage: to express location or direction to a city
restrictions: Some cities have article: Le Caire, La Havane, etc.
conditions: The place is a city, normally used without an article.
À expresses both location in and direction to that city.
agreement_rules: à is invariable; city names normally take no article, so no gender or number agreement applies.
Cities that do carry an article keep it and agree accordingly (Le Caire, La Havane).
common_traps: Do not use en/au for cities.

sources.source_text: With cities, the preposition à is used. Cities are usually not preceded by an article.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Preposition with countries: en, au, aux
grammar_rules.summary: Use en for feminine countries and masculine starting with vowel; au for masculine; aux for plural.
grammar_rules.explanation: Preposition depends on gender and number of country.
grammar_rules.formation: en + feminine or vowel-starting masculine; au + masculine singular; aux + plural
restrictions: à is not used directly before a country name
en is used only for feminine countries and masculine countries beginning with a vowel
Cities take à, not en or au
exceptions: à is not used before country names; cities take à
en is used only for feminine countries and masculine countries beginning with a vowel
agreement_rules: The preposition reflects the country's gender and number: en + feminine or vowel-initial masculine, au + masculine singular, aux + plural.
Contracted forms au (à + le) and aux (à + les) show the country's gender and number.
common_traps: Do not use à for countries.

sources.source_text: en before feminine countries and regions; en before masculine countries beginning with a vowel; au before singular masculine countries; aux before plural countries.

concepts.name: geographical names
concepts.description: Use of articles and prepositions with countries, cities, etc.

sources.source_text: Countries, continents, states, provinces, and regions also have a gender.
